title: Niche topics people miss
objectives: Explain drawdowns, commitment vs invested, valuation lag and fees-on-fees.
Say why overlap must be checked across all three products.
body_md:
These are the comparison details that most often get missed.

| Topic | What to explain | Investor takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drawdowns (capital calls) | In many Cat I & II AIFs, the commitment is drawn in stages over months or years, not invested upfront. | Keep committed money ready; missing a call can have penalties. |
| Commitment vs invested | Returns are often quoted on money actually invested, while the client thinks of the full commitment. | Ask how returns are calculated. |
| J-curve | Early years of a private equity or VC AIF often look flat or negative. | Judge over the fund's full life. |
| Valuation lag | Unlisted holdings are valued periodically using estimates, so AIF NAVs can look smoother than they really are. | Smooth isn't the same as low-risk. |
| Category III tax | Cat III AIFs are generally taxed at fund level, which can affect post-tax returns compared with PMS or MFs. | Compare post-tax, with your CA. |
| Private placement | AIFs cannot be publicly advertised; social media "AIF offers" should be treated with caution. | Only invest via SEBI-registered intermediaries. |
| Minimum for employees | A manager's employees and directors can invest from ₹25 lakh, not ₹1 crore. | The ₹1 crore minimum applies to other investors. |
| Overlap across products | A client's MF, PMS and Cat III AIF may all hold the same large listed stocks. | Check overlap across all three, not within each. |
| Fees on fees | Fund-of-funds AIFs add a second layer of fees. | Ask for the all-in cost. |
example: Fund-of-funds AIF: two layers of fees — ask for the all-in cost before comparing with a mutual fund's single expense ratio.
say: Smooth isn't the same as low-risk.
Check overlap across all three products, not within each.
never: AIF NAV smoothness means low risk.
Returns are always quoted on the full commitment.

check.q: Category III AIFs are generally taxed:
o: In the investor's hands on every trade
Only on exit, at slab rate
check.why: Cat I & II have pass-through status for most income.

o: Overlap only matters within one product
